question: Gaurav bought the first pen for ₹444 and the second pen for ₹356, respectively. He sells the first pen at 75% of the profit but the buyer bargains for the price, and he has to offer a 14% discount and the second pen at 48% of the profit. Find the total profit he had in this transaction (correct to two decimal places).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit on **First Pen**: Let **Marked Price** be CP × (1 + 0.75). Net SP = MP × (1 − 0.14).

Effective Profit 1 = 444 × [1.75 × 0.86 − 1] = 444 × 0.505 = 224.22.

Profit on **Second Pen** = 356 × 48% = 356 × 0.48 = 170.88.

Total Profit = 224.22 + 170.88 = 395.10.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹395.10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **CP₁** = ₹444, **Mark-up** = 75%, **Discount** = 14%, **CP₂** = ₹356, **Profit%₂** = 48%.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 × (100 − D%) ÷ 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/04c93b42035a7bc2689095af244446876305bed2c8b278c2bccc1f5b3c4a8376.png] 
⇒ For the **first pen**, Mark-up Price = 444 + (75% of 444) = 444 + 333 = ₹777.
⇒ Selling Price of first pen = 777 − (14% of 777) = 777 − 108.78 = ₹668.22.
⇒ Profit from first pen = 668.22 − 444 = ₹224.22.
⇒ Profit from the **second pen** = 48% of 356 = 0.48 × 356 = ₹170.88.
⇒ Total Profit = 224.22 + 170.88 = ₹395.10.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹395.10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Profit Percentage

When a markup (m%) and then a discount (d%) is applied, the net profit% is given by the formula: [m − d − (m × d) ÷ 100].

Marked Price and Selling Price

The relationship between CP and SP through MP is SP = CP × (1 + markup%) × (1 − discount%).
